synthesis: Across the time, quadratic-character, and cusp-form settings, the source expands a tunable resonator inside baseline and target-weighted averages, uses the setting's averaging law to reduce those averages to finite quadratic forms, and then compares the target-weighted form with resonator energy. Fourier decay leaves equality and mk=n incidences, discriminant averaging leaves odd-square products, and Petersson orthogonality, after Hecke multiplication, leaves a diagonal energy form and a gcd-sensitive target kernel.
source_support: Units u01 and u04 define the zeta moment ratio and derive its Fourier-selected coefficient sums. Units u09 and u10 derive the quadratic-family baseline and central-value moments by separating square from nonsquare character products. Units u15 and u17 derive the cusp-form baseline and central-value forms from Petersson's formula and the Hecke relation. No single unit supplies this three-setting correspondence.
nonparaphrase_operation: The cross-unit operation is to identify the family-specific orthogonalizer, determine which index relation it preserves, and only then optimize the resulting target-kernel-to-energy ratio; the preserved relation changes from frequency equality or divisibility to square classes to a Hecke-induced gcd kernel.
limits: This is an architectural correspondence, not a shared formula. The three settings have different weights, positivity inputs, admissible lengths, kernels, and off-diagonal errors; the character, Fourier, trace, divisor, cutoff, and normalization formulas are extraction-sensitive and require PDF verification.
quality_reason: Accepted because six distinct units jointly exhibit the same ordered mechanism through three mathematically different averaging laws, while the synthesis states the different surviving kernels and does not infer that one family's estimates transfer verbatim to another.

synthesis: The source repeatedly combines two steps: choose squarefree multiplicative coefficients on a tuned prime window so favorable cross terms become local Euler factors, then use a positive Rankin tilt to compare the finite resonator sums with their factorizable infinite extensions. This pairing supplies the zeta correlation gain, controls the zeta fourth-moment cost, and justifies the quadratic-family and cusp-form product evaluations at their chosen finite lengths.
source_support: Unit u05 constructs f on an intermediate prime window and uses Rankin's trick to retain the Euler-product numerator below n<=N. Unit u08 repeats prime-local factorization for both correlation and fourth-moment cost with a V-dependent coefficient scale. Units u12 and u14 separately remove the first- and second-moment cutoff tails in the quadratic family, including the coprime a,r,s factorization. Unit u18 invokes the same finite-to-product passage for the cusp-form baseline and central moment.
nonparaphrase_operation: Sparse squarefree support turns global coefficient sums into a small set of prime-local states, while exponential tilting replaces a hard length cutoff by a weighted tail whose ratio to the desired Euler product can be bounded; the local optimization and the finite-range certification are distinct but coupled steps.
limits: The argument applies to the displayed coefficient choices and admissible parameter ranges, not arbitrary multiplicative weights or arbitrarily long resonators. Prime windows, tilts, local factors, PNT asymptotics, family errors, and cutoff exponents are formula-sensitive. In u18 the f large-value product is displayed, whereas the mu f small-value completion is only stated.
quality_reason: Accepted because the zeta, quadratic-character, and cusp-form units jointly support a concrete reusable construction-and-tail-removal mechanism, with repeated explicit Rankin bounds rather than a generic appeal to multiplicativity.

synthesis: In both the quadratic-character and cusp-form families, the untwisted coefficient choice f gives constructive prime-level correlation for a large-value witness, while replacing f by mu f reverses the linear prime contribution and supplies the small-value witness. The quadratic-family unit displays the negative local factor for mu f and states the f counterpart; the cusp-form unit displays the positive local factor for f and states the mu f counterpart.
source_support: Unit u11 gives the quadratic-family products: the baseline has factors 1+f(p)^2 and the mu f target moment has factors with -2f(p)/sqrt(p), producing a small weighted ratio; it then directs the f choice for large values. Unit u18 gives the cusp-form baseline and the f target product with +2f(p)/sqrt(p), then directs the mu f choice for small values. Their conjunction establishes the same sign-selection mechanism in two different family averages.
nonparaphrase_operation: Möbius twisting changes the sign of the prime-local cross term without changing the coefficient magnitudes, so Euler factorization separates amplitude control from correlation direction and recombines the local bias into an extreme weighted ratio in each family.
limits: Each conclusion is an existence consequence of its weighted-average setup, not an explicit family member and not a claim that every central value is positive or nonzero. Each unit displays only one sign direction and states the reverse direction; local factors, constants, scales, and the needed positivity or absolute-value inference require their surrounding proof and PDF-level formula verification.
quality_reason: Accepted because the two parent units provide complementary, family-specific Euler products whose linear terms concretely realize the same sign-modulation operation; the synthesis preserves which direction is displayed and which is only asserted.

synthesis: The usable resonator length is governed by the highest moment and the ambient orthogonality error that must be controlled. The zeta maximum uses the near-full N=T^(1-epsilon) diagonal quadratic ratio, the moderate-frequency regime can bypass a tuned resonator using the second and fourth zeta moments, and the rarer-value argument shortens to N<=T^(1/2-epsilon) so the resonator fourth moment is diagonal. Quadratic-character errors and the Petersson-Bessel range impose their own family-specific length restrictions.
source_support: Unit u04 derives the zeta quadratic ratio only under N<=T^(1-epsilon), and u07 uses that near-full length for the maximum while using ordinary second/fourth moments for moderate superlevel sets. Unit u08 introduces a resonator fourth moment for larger V and requires N<=T^(1/2-epsilon) to suppress ab!=cd. Unit u10 displays a quadratic-family error growing with resonator size, while u15 permits Petersson diagonalization only in its stated short-index range.
nonparaphrase_operation: Changing the requested output from one extreme value to the frequency of rarer values changes the controlling moment from resonator energy to a resonator fourth moment, enlarges the index products that must be diagonalized, and therefore tightens the length budget; other families obtain analogous budgets from character-sum or trace-formula errors.
limits: The numerical ranges belong to different ambient parameters and should not be treated as a universal ordering or barrier for extreme L-values. The moderate and rare V regimes use different arguments, and all threshold, exponent, Bessel, character-error, and normalization formulas are extraction-sensitive and require PDF verification.
quality_reason: Accepted because five units jointly show a concrete dependency between evaluation method, moment order, off-diagonal control, and admissible length, including a genuine regime change from maximum detection to frequency bounds rather than a generic efficiency tradeoff.
